observation_kind: targeted current official NPD lifecycle, planning-location/pagination, first-return/time-stamped LIDAR and contour/shapefile checks; not independent bulk HTTP fetches
rules: The National Polygon Dataset is HM Land Registry's published collection of Index Polygons for England and Wales.
On completion of a registered title, HMLR normally produces a title plan, a register and one or more index polygons.
The title plan and register record the general boundary position unless an exact boundary has been determined.
An index polygon forms part of the statutory index and indicates the location of a registered title.
The title number allows National Polygon records to link to Title Descriptor and UPRN products.
INSPIRE Index Polygons are a subset of the National Polygon Dataset.
The INSPIRE subset carries simpler attributes for identifier, creation date and last-updated date.
Shape is mandatory and the index-polygon geometry must be a single area.
Poly_ID is a mandatory numeric field and is the unique polygon reference.
Poly_ID uniqueness is managed through dataset lifecycle rules.
Title_No is a mandatory character field identifying the registered title.
INSERT is a mandatory date recording when the polygon was initially created on the index map.
UPDATE is a mandatory date recording when all or part of the title polygon was last updated.
Vers_No is a mandatory numeric field recording the version of Poly_ID.
Rec_Status is a mandatory character field describing polygon status.
The National Polygon record-status values are Added, Changed and Deleted, represented by A, C and D.
The title number is a unique identifier suitable for linking National Polygon records to other HMLR data.
The Planning Data API exposes more than 100 planning and housing datasets through one consistent interface.
A latitude-and-longitude query returns entities whose geometry intersects the supplied point.
Multiple dataset parameters return matching entities from any of the selected datasets covering the point.
Documented entity responses include name, dataset, start-date, geometry and point fields.
An empty result must not be presented as proof that no constraints exist because coverage varies by area.
The documentation describes fetching all 337 local planning authorities in one request.
The LPA discovery example restricts output to name and entity fields with a limit of 500.
geometry_entity can apply an existing entity's geometry, such as an LPA boundary, to a spatial filter.
Raw polygon filters use WKT, and spaces in the WKT must be percent-encoded in the request.
Geometry-query coordinates are documented as WGS84, EPSG:4326.
For pagination, offset is incremented by the selected limit for each subsequent page.
Entity responses include pre-built next, previous, first and last pagination links.
The 1m first-return composite DSM covers approximately 99 percent of England.
The first-return DSM uses the first or only laser pulse returned to the sensor.
The first-return DSM includes vehicles, buildings and vegetation, plus terrain where the first or only return was ground.
Its source surveys were captured by the National LIDAR Programme from 11 November 2016 to 5 May 2022.
The programme divided England into approximately 300 survey blocks.
The survey programme operated across continuous winter capture seasons from 2016 onward.
Survey overlaps are merged with feathering to reduce small elevation differences between surveys.
First-return composite coverage and extent do not necessarily match the last-return DSM composite.
The product is supplied as GeoTIFF rasters in 5km tiles aligned to the OS National Grid.
Elevations are in metres, referenced to Ordnance Survey Newlyn and transformed using OSTN15.
Input surveys have stated vertical accuracy of plus or minus 15cm RMSE.
The metadata record exposes WMS, WCS, WMTS and OGC API Features service surfaces.
The time-stamped DSM archive contains site-specific Environment Agency surveys carried out since 1998.
Some areas, including the coastal zone, have been surveyed multiple times.
Time-stamped DSM data can be available at 25cm, 50cm, 1m or 2m resolution.
The archived DSM is produced from the last-return LIDAR signal and includes terrain and surface objects.
The archive is delivered as GeoTIFF rasters in 5km ZIP packages.
Data is aligned to the OS Grid, measured in metres and referenced to Ordnance Survey Newlyn.
The transformation used for time-stamped data depends on the survey period.
The metadata catalogue identifies survey dates, product resolution, transformation and geoidal model for a location.
Environment Agency survey data is supplied in OSGB36 British National Grid.
Elevations are recorded above Ordnance Datum Newlyn.
The LIDAR Composite is transformed using the OSTN15 geoid model.
Surveys after 26 August 2016 use the OSGM15 geoid model.
OS Terrain 50 contour layers are supplied in GML 3.2.1.
Processing the GML supply may require understanding XML and XML schemas.
Each contour tile includes a GML data file named from the tile reference.
Each contour tile includes an XML metadata file carrying information such as flying date.
Spot heights are selected automatically as the highest mass point within every closed contour.
A selected point is removed when its height equals the enclosing contour.
A spot height can be lower than its surrounding contour where a genuine depression exists.
OS Terrain 50 contour spot-height z values are rounded to zero decimal places.
The Esri shapefile supply is a simple non-topological format for feature geometry and attributes.
The .shx component stores the feature-geometry index.
The .dbf component stores feature attributes as a dBASE table.
Tile line-layer files contain contour and tide-line data.
Tile point-layer files contain spot-height data.
